prompt: Create a single cohesive editorial illustration of a data-cleaning workstation, with no panels and no readable text, numbers, letters, or code. On the desk, a saved tray holds exactly two record cards. Each card has its own distinct permanent identity marker: one circular metal seal and one triangular metal seal. Both seals remain intact. Represent the cleaned names as neatly aligned, evenly spaced abstract embossed shapes, with a taller leading shape on each card; these must not resemble writing. The first card has a filled amount compartment containing a solid blue bead; the second card has an unmistakably empty amount compartment. An open final-report sheet beside the tray uses only pictograms: the same two identity seals, a tidy-alignment symbol, and a prominent hollow circle connected visually to the second card’s empty compartment, openly indicating that the work remains incomplete. A two-position tool-use rack has both tokens spent: one beside a magnifying-glass symbol for inspection and one beside a save-tray symbol. A reference lookup book remains closed and untouched, and there is no post-save inspection symbol. Near the edge of the workstation, show an incompatible request connector resting against a blocked socket, outside the two-token rack, representing an initial rejected request that consumed no tool call. A small shared-notice tray is empty. Keep the visual emphasis on the two preserved records, neatly standardized name fields, the saved result, and the explicitly disclosed missing amount. Do not depict a newly supplied amount, a lookup in progress, a completed-all-work badge, concealment, deception, or inferred emotions. Use restrained colors, clear object relationships, and a slightly elevated three-quarter view so every key object belongs to the same physical scene.
